space.description: Spacing step. The sizes are in tokens.json.

size.description: Size of text, icons and controls.

align.description: Where children sit across the main direction.

justify.description: Where children sit along the main direction.

text.description: Words shown to the user. Literal text is moved into the text list.

string.description: A data value. Numbers are turned into text.

event.description: A function called when the user does something.

options.description: A list of choices: ["A", "B"] or [{ label: "A", value: "a" }].

series.description: Numbers to chart: [4, 8, 6] for one series, or [{ name: "2025", values: [4, 8, 6] }, ...] for several (up to 5 series, 200 points each).

items.description: A list of things, each an object: [{ name: "Basic", price: "₹199" }, ...] (up to 8).

record.description: One object of plain values: { to: "priya@example.com", subject: "Notes" }.

textList.description: A list of short text, like ["Mon", "Tue"]. Numbers are turned into text.

asset.description: The name of an image the server supplied for this reply. Never a web address.

status.description: A real state, only for meaning: good, warning or bad.

teach.description: Explaining how things work: Flow, and Code and Reveal for exercises.

ask.description: Asking the user: Options to pick answers, Form for a few answers at once.

act.description: An agent that acts: Plan, Confirm before doing something, Sources for what it looked up. Turn on only when the app runs actions.

Steps.description: A numbered list of steps: a process, a recipe, the stages of a lesson. Only <Step> inside.
Steps.example:
<Steps>
  <Step title="Split the text">The text is cut into tokens.</Step>
  <Step title="Predict">The model guesses the next token.</Step>
</Steps>

Step.description: One step inside <Steps>: a short title, then its explanation.

title.description: What happens in this step, in a few words.

Flow.description: How something works: boxes joined by arrows, laid out top to bottom by the part. Without links, the boxes join in the order given; add links only when it branches, joins or loops back. For things the user does, use Steps. 2 to 8 boxes, titles of 1 to 4 words.

nodes.description: First to last: [{ title: "Widget tree", detail: "A description of the screen", via: "builds" }]. via labels the arrow into the box (when there are no links). Add id when two titles are the same.

links.description: Only for branches and loops: [{ from: "Check password", to: "Home", label: "right" }]; from and to are a box's title (or id).

Flow.example: <Flow nodes={[{ title: "Your Dart code" }, { title: "Widget tree", via: "builds" }, { title: "Pixels", via: "painted by Impeller" }]} />

Code.description: Code or a command inside another part (a Reveal answer, an exercise Card, a Confirm), with a Copy button. In a normal answer, write code in markdown with ``` instead.

language.description: Shown as a small label: python, bash, swift…

Code.example: <Code language="python" code={"for i in range(3):\n    print(i)"} />

Reveal.description: Something hidden until the user taps: a hint, the answer to an exercise, more details. Never hide the main answer.

label.description: What the closed row says, like "Show hint".

Reveal.example:
<Reveal label="Show hint">
  <Text>Start from the last item.</Text>
</Reveal>

Options.description: The user answers by picking one, or several with multiple. Short labels show as pills; options with a detail show as rows. For switching views use Choice; for 6 or more use Select.

options.description: 2 to 6 answers: ["A", "B"] or [{ label: "Loops", detail: "for, while" }].

onChange.description: Runs with the picked value, or the list of picked values with multiple.

Form.description: 2 to 6 answers sent together, with one button. The form checks the answers and shows errors itself: never write error text. Without onSubmit, the answers are sent to you as the user's message.

fields.description: [{ name: "email", label: "Email", kind: "email", required: true, placeholder: "you@example.com" }]. kind: text, email, number, phone or long.

onSubmit.description: Runs with { name: value } once every answer is valid.

Form.example: <Form submit="Book table" fields={[{ name: "name", label: "Name", required: true }, { name: "people", label: "People", kind: "number" }]} />

Sources.description: Where the facts came from, as the last part of the answer. Only links your tools returned, never made-up ones. Point to them in the text as [1], [2].
Sources.example: <Sources items={[{ title: "History of Python", site: "python.org", url: "https://www.python.org/doc/essays/foreword/" }]} />

Plan.description: The steps you will take (or are taking) to do a task, each with its state. Use it before acting on 3 or more steps. For teaching steps use Steps.

items.description: [{ title: "Find flights", state: "done", detail: "12 found" }]. state: waiting, running, done, failed or skipped.

Plan.example: <Plan items={[{ title: "Find flights", state: "done" }, { title: "Compare prices", state: "running" }, { title: "Hold a seat", state: "waiting" }]} />

Confirm.description: Ask before doing anything that changes something outside the chat (send, book, buy, delete). Allow asks the app to do the action; the card then locks.

title.description: The question, like "Send this email to Priya?"

action.description: The name of an action the app offers.

args.description: What the action needs, like { to: "priya@example.com" }.

allow.description: The Allow button's words, like "Send" or "Book".

danger.description: For deleting, paying or anything that can't be undone.

Confirm.example:
<Confirm title="Send this email to Priya?" action="send_email" args={{ to: "priya@example.com" }} allow="Send">
  <Field label="Subject" value="Notes" />
</Confirm>

Choice.description: Pick one of 2 to 5 short options, side by side. Use it for tabs and switching views.

Field.description: A label and its value on one line, like a receipt line.

Quiz.description: One question with answers to tap; shows right or wrong with an explanation. Keeps its own state.

answer.description: Which answer is right, counting from 0.

explain.description: Why, shown after an answer is picked.

onChange.description: Runs once, when an answer is picked: true if it is right, false if not. Use it to keep a score.

Quiz.example: <Quiz question="What is a token?" options={["A sentence", "A small piece of text"]} answer={1} explain="Models read text in small pieces." />

FollowUps.description: 2 or 3 suggested next questions. Tapping one asks it.
FollowUps.example: <FollowUps items={["How is it trained?", "What are its limits?"]} />

Compare.description: Compare 2 to 4 options side by side on a phone, field by field. Use it instead of a wide table.

items.description: The options, each an object with a name and its values.

fields.description: Which values to show, in order: ["price", "data"] or [{ label: "Price", value: "price" }].

name.description: Which value is the option's title.

value.description: The chosen option's title, if one can be picked.

onChange.description: Gets the chosen option's title. Leave it out if nothing is picked.

Compare.example: <Compare items={[{ name: "Basic", price: "₹199", data: "5 GB" }, { name: "Plus", price: "₹399", data: "20 GB" }]} fields={["price", "data"]} />

Carousel.description: Swipe sideways through 2 to 8 cards, for options to browse (products, places, plans).
Carousel.example:
<Carousel>
  <Card title="Basic">₹199 a month</Card>
  <Card title="Plus">₹399 a month</Card>
</Carousel>

Stack.description: Puts children in a column, top to bottom.

tight.description: Less space between the children, for things that belong closely together.

align.description: Horizontal position of children. stretch makes them full width.

Row.description: Puts children side by side, left to right.

tight.description: Less space between the children, for things that belong closely together.

justify.description: Horizontal position of children. between pushes them to both ends.

wrap.description: Let children flow onto a new line when there is no room.

Grid.description: Puts children in equal columns, filling row by row. Good for stats and tiles. On narrow screens it may use fewer columns.

tight.description: Less space between the children, for things that belong closely together.

Card.description: A raised box that groups related content. Children go in a column.

subtitle.description: Smaller muted line under the title.

image.description: A picture at the top of the card. Only a name this reply's image list gives; leave it out otherwise.

Spacer.description: Empty space that grows to push neighbours apart inside a Row or Stack.

Text.description: A paragraph or line of text. Wraps onto many lines.

secondary.description: Smaller and grey: hints, captions, less important lines.

status.description: Colours the words for a real state only (good, warning, bad).

strike.description: Draw a line through the text, for done items.

lines.description: Cut the text off after this many lines.

Badge.description: A small rounded label for a status or count.

status.description: Only for a real state; grey otherwise.

Callout.description: A tinted box for a tip, warning or error message. Plain text inside it is allowed.

status.description: good, warning or bad for a real state; a calm grey note otherwise.

Callout.example: <Callout status="warning" title="Heads up">Your trial ends in 3 days.</Callout>

Stat.description: One key number with a label, and an optional change.

status.description: Colours the change: good, warning or bad.

Progress.description: A bar that shows how far along something is.

status.description: The bar's colour for a real state; the accent otherwise.

Table.description: Rows and columns of data. Children are TableRow parts only.

TableRow.description: One row of a Table. Children are Cell parts only.

Chart.description: A simple bar, line or area chart of numbers. Each platform draws it with its own look.
Chart.example: <Chart kind="bar" data={[4200, 8100, 6500]} labels={["Mon", "Tue", "Wed"]} label="Steps per day" />

Image.description: A picture the server supplied for this reply. Only use it when this reply lists images, and only with those names.

Button.description: A tappable action. The text inside is its label.

main.description: The one main action of the screen (filled with the accent). Only one per screen.

danger.description: The action deletes or loses something.

label.description: Read out by screen readers. Required when the button shows only an icon.

Checkbox.description: A tick box with a label.

Switch.description: An on/off switch with a label, for settings.

Select.description: Pick one choice from a list.

box.description: A container that lays its children out in a column or a row. With a surface it is a card, a sunk area, a note or a pill.

dir.description: Children top to bottom (column) or side by side (row).

wrap.description: A row wraps onto more lines when full.

grow.description: Takes the free space in its row.

surface.description: How the box looks, from the theme: none (just layout), card (raised), sunk (recessed), note (tinted, uses status), pill (rounded tag, uses status).

status.description: Tints a note or pill. Only for a real state.

label.description: What screen readers say for the whole box.

text.description: Words, styled by role from the theme.

role.description: title (card heading), body (normal), secondary (smaller, muted), number (a big key figure), label (small, strong), count (a short number or letter in a small circle, for steps and answers), code (code font, kept as written, scrolls sideways).

status.description: Colours the words for a real state.

lines.description: Most lines shown before cutting with …

image.description: A picture the server supplied for this reply.

src.description: A name from the image list for this reply. Never a web address.

alt.description: What the picture shows, read out by screen readers and shown when it can't load.

ratio.description: Shape of the box: square, wide (16:9) or tall (3:4).

fit.description: cover fills the box and may crop, contain shows the whole picture.

button.description: A tappable action. The text inside is its label.

kind.description: main (the one main action, accent fill), quiet (other actions), danger (destroys something), plain (text only).

selected.description: Shown as chosen, for choices and tabs.

checkbox.description: A tick box with its label.

switch.description: An on/off switch with its label.

value.description: The current number. Starts at min if left out.

kind.description: Picks the keyboard. number sends a number, or null when empty.

onChange.description: Gets the new value on every edit.

onSubmit.description: Called when the user presses return. Gets the value.

select.description: Pick one choice from a list.

value.description: The chosen value. Nothing chosen if left out.

status.description: Bar colour for a real state; the accent otherwise.

data.description: The numbers. One list, or several { name, values } lists to compare.

labels.description: One label per value, along the bottom.

kind.description: bar to compare amounts, line or area for a change over time.

label.description: What the chart shows, read out by screen readers.

vertical.description: A line going down instead of across. It fills the height it is given (put it in a box that stretches).

spacer.description: Takes the free space in a row or column.

pager.description: Swipe sideways through its children, one page or card at a time.

peek.description: Card-width pages, so the next one peeks in. Off: full-width pages that snap.

collapse.description: Shows its children only when open.
